answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making reputation a slow-accruing, non-transferable stake. Each new identity posts collateral that unlocks only as its work survives repeated peer audits, progress accumulating as gradually as a glacier. A would-be attacker must push every puppet up the same steep cost ridge, funding thousands of umber-marked ledger entries that cannot be merged or refunded quickly. Because clones inherit no history and collateral thaws on schedule, the attacker expense grows linearly per fake identity while one honest agent compounds a single durable record.
